messages:
maria: Heads-up — canary apply of Cilium 1.14 in eu-west-1-gpu is flapping. kube-system pods CrashLoopBackOff, a bunch of nodes reporting ENI/IP exhaustion on three subnets. Thinking rollback the canary and pause GitOps.

devin: Seen similar when nodegroup ASG replaced without propagated subnet tags — new instances couldn't attach ENIs. Any terraform plan drift?

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/cilium-1-14 started by @maria (sha: a1b2c3). Canary target: nodepool-gpu-eu1 (10% of nodes).

liam: Paste from one of the kubelet logs:
```
Kubelet: failed to assign IP to pod "cilium-agent-xxxxx": no available IPs in subnet-0a1b2c3 (used 255/256)
ENI attach error: AttachNetworkInterface failed: Network interface limit exceeded for instance
```

jen: Quick check — did the helm chart upgrade include hostPort changes? Cilium's DaemonSet might be requesting extra host ports which pushes IP allocations on ENI-based CNI. Also CRD migration ordering can pause agent init.

ops-runner: Terraform plan from earlier shows nodegroup replacement due to launch_template_name change:
```
~ module.nodegroups.aws_autoscaling_group.gpu
  -/+ (forces new resource)
```
No subnet tag propagation in the new launch template either (we tag subnets in tf module via aws_subnet_ids -> map). If new instances spin up in a subnet with low free IPs we hit the limit.

maria: I'm going to pause the ArgoCD app for cilium (canary) and scale the canary set to 0 so traffic falls back. Can someone verify ENI quotas in account and the three subnets' free IPs? If quota is fine we may need to drain the least-used AZ first.

devin: Running quick checks:
- aws ec2 describe-instances: new instances are in subnet-0a1b2c3 (eu-west-1a) which is at 98% IP usage.
- Account ENI quota: 2000/2000 (we're at limit in this account for non-burst).

liam: Oof quota hit. Options: request soft-limit increase (slow), shift canary to other AZs, or reduce pods requesting hostNetwork/hostPort. For immediate mitigation: scale down cilium canary, revert helm values that changed hostPort, and kick nodes to drain from the most-full subnet.

jen: Suggestion: patch canary values to disable hostPort and disable nodeinit that creates extra interfaces. Example patch: `helm upgrade --reuse-values --set global.hostPort.enabled=false` — apply only to canary release.

ops-runner: Also found a GitOps ordering bug — CRDs are applied after the daemonset in the generated manifests due to our manifest generator sorting. That will cause init failures on startup and retries, leaving pods stuck while they keep consuming ENI attachments. Need to add a hook to apply CRDs first.

maria: I've paused ArgoCD and scaled the canary down to 0. Will open a support request to AWS for ENI quota increase, but that's not immediate.

devin: Filing a short postmortem ticket with action items:
- add pre-apply step to ensure CRDs are present before DaemonSet
- add subnet free-ip check in our canary gating pipeline
- fix launch_template tag propagation in TF module to ensure instances land in healthy subnets
- add per-account ENI quota monitor alert

maria: Thanks — for now we rolled back the canary and set a temporary gitops guard. Reassigning follow-ups to ops-runner + devex to add gating. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/cilium-1-14 rolled back by @maria (reason: ENI/IP exhaustion).
